systems.d: Skin and cutaneous appendages (hair). The largest organ of the body: it protects against physical, chemical and microbial aggression, regulates temperature and houses sensory receptors.
Skeletal muscles, tendons, aponeuroses and associated ligaments. They produce movement, maintain posture and generate heat. The human body has more than 600 skeletal muscles.

Bones, cartilages and intervertebral discs. The adult skeleton has about 206 bones: it supports the body, protects organs, acts as a lever for muscles, stores calcium and phosphorus and houses the hematopoietic bone marrow.
Brain, optic pathways, ventricular system and sense organs. It integrates sensory information and coordinates the body's responses.
Heart and great vessels. At rest the heart pumps about 5 litres of blood per minute through the systemic and pulmonary circulations.
Airways and lungs. They allow the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide between air and blood.
Digestive tract from the mouth to the anus and accessory glands (liver, gallbladder, pancreas). It digests food and absorbs nutrients and water.
Kidneys, ureters, bladder and urethra. It filters the blood, regulates fluid-electrolyte and acid-base balance and eliminates waste in the urine.
Testes, spermatic ducts, accessory glands and penis. The source model (BodyParts3D) corresponds to an adult male.
Glands that release hormones into the blood. In this model: pituitary gland, pineal gland and adrenal glands.
Lymphoid organs: spleen and thymus. They take part in immune defence and, in the case of the spleen, in filtering the blood.

concepts.d: Branch of the left coronary artery that descends in the anterior interventricular groove. It supplies the anterior surface of both ventricles and the anterior 2/3 of the septum. The coronary arteries supply the myocardium itself; their obstruction causes ischaemia and infarction.

concepts.n: Circumflex branch of the left coronary artery
concepts.d: It runs in the left coronary groove to the posterior surface of the heart and supplies the atrium and the lateral wall of the left ventricle. The coronary arteries supply the myocardium itself; their obstruction causes ischaemia and infarction.
Branch of the celiac trunk that runs along the lesser curvature of the stomach and gives off oesophageal branches.

concepts.n: Inferior lobe of the left lung
concepts.d: Lobe below the oblique fissure of the left lung; it forms most of the diaphragmatic and posterior surfaces. The lungs contain ≈300–500 million alveoli, with an exchange surface of ≈70 m².

concepts.n: Inferior lobe of the right lung
concepts.d: Basal and posterior lobe of the right lung, below the oblique fissure. It has five segments (superior and four basal). The lungs contain ≈300–500 million alveoli, with an exchange surface of ≈70 m².

Branch of the right coronary artery that descends along the right (acute) margin of the heart and supplies the right ventricle. The coronary arteries supply the myocardium itself; their obstruction causes ischaemia and infarction.

concepts.n: Middle lobe of the right lung
concepts.d: Lobe exclusive to the right lung, bounded by the horizontal and oblique fissures. It has two segments: lateral and medial. The lungs contain ≈300–500 million alveoli, with an exchange surface of ≈70 m².

It descends in the posterior interventricular groove and supplies the posterior third of the septum and the inferior surface of the ventricles. It arises from the right coronary artery in ≈80 % of people (right dominance). The coronary arteries supply the myocardium itself; their obstruction causes ischaemia and infarction.

concepts.n: Posterior papillary muscle of the left ventricle
concepts.d: Projection of the left ventricular myocardium attached by chordae tendineae to the cusps of the mitral valve. It prevents their prolapse during systole.

concepts.n: Posterior papillary muscle of the right ventricle
concepts.d: Projection of the right ventricular myocardium attached by chordae tendineae to the tricuspid valve. It prevents their prolapse during systole.

Terminal branch of the right coronary artery that supplies the posterolateral surface of the left ventricle. The coronary arteries supply the myocardium itself; their obstruction causes ischaemia and infarction.

concepts.n: Septal branches of the left coronary artery
concepts.d: Branches of the anterior interventricular artery that penetrate the anterior 2/3 of the interventricular septum, where the conduction system runs. The coronary arteries supply the myocardium itself; their obstruction causes ischaemia and infarction.

concepts.n: Septal branches of the right coronary artery
concepts.d: Small branches that penetrate the posterior third of the interventricular septum. The coronary arteries supply the myocardium itself; their obstruction causes ischaemia and infarction.

concepts.n: Posterior veins of the left ventricle
concepts.d: They drain the diaphragmatic surface of the left ventricle into the coronary sinus.

It arises from the left aortic sinus and, after a short course (≈1 cm), divides into the anterior interventricular and circumflex branches. The coronary arteries supply the myocardium itself; their obstruction causes ischaemia and infarction.

It arises from the right aortic sinus and runs in the right coronary groove. It supplies the right atrium and ventricle and, in most people, the sinoatrial and atrioventricular nodes. The coronary arteries supply the myocardium itself; their obstruction causes ischaemia and infarction.

concepts.n: Superior lobe of the left lung
concepts.d: Upper lobe of the left lung. It includes the lingula, equivalent to the right middle lobe, and the cardiac notch that leaves room for the heart. The lungs contain ≈300–500 million alveoli, with an exchange surface of ≈70 m².

concepts.n: Superior lobe of the right lung
concepts.d: Apical lobe of the right lung, separated from the middle lobe by the horizontal fissure. It has three segments: apical, posterior and anterior. The lungs contain ≈300–500 million alveoli, with an exchange surface of ≈70 m².
